title: Chapter 2728: More Time
content:
Chapter 2728: More Time

"Its name is—" Yu Rou revealed the Eternal’s name.

However, Yuan looked puzzled afterward.

"Sorry, but can you say that again?"

"Its name is—"

Yu Rou repeated the name, but to Yuan it sounded like gibberish, reminding him of the first time he’d heard Xiao Hua recite Heaven’s Secret Art to him.

’Am I unable to hear its name for whatever reason, or is it spoken in a language that I don’t understand?’ he wondered inwardly.

"What’s wrong?" Yu Rou eventually asked him.

Yuan told her the truth—that he couldn’t understand the name.

"You can’t comprehend it? I’m not speaking in another language, either," Yu Rou revealed, confirming Yuan’s initial suspicion.

"I guess I am not permitted to learn its name," Yuan sighed aloud.

"Does knowing its name really matter?" Yu Rou then asked. "Will it help us with the invaders?"

"Well... it’s important information, but it probably won’t help our situation. Anyways, can you write its name down for me? I want to see if that would allow me to see it."

Yu Rou nodded, pointed a finger at the ground, and wrote words on it with Limitless.

"..."

Yuan stared at the ground, dumbfounded.

"Well? Can you read it?" Yu Rou asked.

Yuan shook his head and sighed, "The words are all distorted. I have a feeling the Eternal doesn’t want me to know its identity on purpose."

"Forget it. What else did it tell you?"

"It told me that it’d give us more time..." she said, sounding a little confused herself.

"What? More time?" Yuan raised an eyebrow.

"I am having trouble understanding it myself," she sighed.

Yuan turned to look toward the sky and said, "Perhaps it’s trying to tell you that it’ll keep the invaders at bay for a little longer. However, if it really has the capability to do that..."

Yuan didn’t finish the sentence, but his implication was clear.

If the Eternal behind Gaia could strengthen the barrier at will, why did it allow the invaders to break it in the first place?

Did it deliberately let the invaders onto Earth? For what reason?

"I don’t like what you’re implying..." Yu Rou said a moment later, frowning underneath her veil.

"The fact that you know what I am implying says enough," Yuan said, shrugging.

"In the first place, we don’t even know if the Eternal is behind the barrier," Yu Rou said.

As Yu Rou uttered those words, the entire world suddenly darkened, prompting those who had finally managed to tear their eyes away to look back at the sky.

"Heavens!"

Countless cries rang out as they witnessed a massive hand descending upon their world.

BANG!

The hand—likely belonging to the gigantic head they had seen earlier—slammed into the world. In that instant, everyone saw their lives flash before their eyes. Yet, to their surprise, the barrier not only withstood the attack but also repelled it.

In fact, the barrier had suddenly become so powerful that it completely absorbed the impact of the attack, preventing even the earthquakes that would normally follow.

Seeing this, Yuan said aloud, "I guess we can safely assume that the barrier was created by the Eternal, and that it has the ability to strengthen it at will. As for why it waited until now... we can only assume."

Yu Rou gritted her teeth in frustration. She understood what Yuan was implying, and even she couldn’t help but feel puzzled by the Eternal’s actions.

However, she had followed the voice and revered it almost like a god for several thousand years. It wasn’t easy for her to suddenly consider the possibility that it might be trying to harm humanity—or their world.

Eventually, she said, "I cannot tell you why it strengthened the barrier now and not prior to the invasion, but I can tell you that it’s definitely trying to help us. Otherwise, why would it even create the barrier in the first place? Why warn us about the invasion at all?"

Yuan sighed and said, "I’m not saying it’s trying to harm us, but it definitely has ulterior motives, so it’s better to be safe than sorry."

"I’ll keep that in mind."

"In any case, we’ve been given extra time to prepare for the invasion. As for how much time and whether it’d actually make a difference..." Yuan said a moment later.

"Hell, even if we’re given another thousand years to prepare, it won’t matter if nobody has the will to fight."

"Then what do you suggest we do?"

"That’s for you guys to figure out. I already have enough on my plate as it is."

"...You’re right. We can’t rely on you for everything, especially when it’s something we can handle ourselves. I’m sorry," Yu Rou apologized, realizing how selfish it had been to ask even more of Yuan when they had already placed the heaviest responsibility imaginable on his shoulders.

"You don’t have to apologize."

"Then can I ask you what you’re going to do now?"

"What I’m going to do, huh? That’s a good—"

In the middle of his sentence, Yuan suddenly felt lightheaded, and his vision faded to white, as though he were on the verge of losing consciousness.

"Yuan?" Yu Rou called out worriedly when she saw him stagger backward like a drunkard.

"I-I’m fine... I just feel a little..."

Before he could even finish his sentence, Yuan suddenly lost all feeling in his body and fell backward.

"Yuan?!"

The last thing Yuan heard before losing consciousness was Yu Rou’s startled cry.

"..."

"..."

"..."

"Yuan!"

Yuan heard his name being called again shortly after, but it wasn’t Yu Rou’s voice. Though it wasn’t an unfamiliar one, either.

Yuan slowly opened his eyes and found himself lying inside a familiar-looking chamber.

It was an enclosed space that closely resembled the chamber at the end of a tunnel where one would encounter the Void Guardian.

"Huh? How did I get here?" he mumbled in confusion.

"What are you mumbling about?"

The familiar voice asked, prompting Yuan to turn around.

His eyes widened when he saw a white-haired beauty standing behind him.

"M-Mu Xuelian...?"
